ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, senior managers, and ultimate beneficial owners associated with NZ Ltd must be screened against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, New Zealand autonomous sanctions under the Sanctions Act 2022, FATF public statements, Interpol and domestic police adverse media, and the Department of Internal Affairs AML/CFT guidance. Domestic and foreign PEPs, including immediate family members and close associates, require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, and senior management sign-off before incorporation. Non-bank payment rails such as Wise must be treated as covered financial institutions and independently CDD-screened before onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Name Search and Reserve Portal (companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English/Latin alphabet under New Zealand law; no non-Latin transliteration is accepted. Te Reo Māori words may be used, but the name must remain comprehensible in the Latin script and must carry the mandatory suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. The Companies Office applies a four-tier name framework: ordinary distinctive names, names requiring consent, names requiring statutory regulator approval, and prohibited or misleading names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 working days of refusal, the applicant may request reconsideration by the Registrar of Companies under sections 21-22 of the Companies Act 1993, stating why the name is not identical to an existing name and is not misleading. The applicant must attach written consent or approval from any affected statutory authority, and may propose a modified version. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an originating application in the District Court for review while reserving a fallback name to preserve priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Section 34 of the Companies Act 1993 requires a physical registered office address in New Zealand that is not a post-office box or virtual mailbox. A managed office supplied by a reputable corporate service provider can be treated as an acceptable registered office if it is a physical street address and accepts service of process. However, Inland Revenue and New Zealand banks will expect actual surveying substance: an operational workspace, records, claim survey equipment, and a person accountable for business activity. A pure virtual office is likely to be rejected by banks for account opening and may create IRD residency and GST registration challenges for the marine insurance surveying business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspections by Inland Revenue or Companies Office: visible company identification at the address, lease or licence to occupy, utility records, professional indemnity insurance certificates, surveyor qualification evidence, job registers, and health-and-safety notices. Quantified risk is approximately 5-10% per year for a new low-risk single-purpose company; the probability rises above 30% if the registered address is a mere mailbox, if nominee layers are present, or if expense and activity patterns are inconsistent with marine surveying.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 10 (Registrar of Companies), 12 (Application for registration), 13 (Registration of company), 15 (Date of incorporation), 16-21 (Constitution), 39 (Share issues), 42 (Share allotment filings), 101 (Minimum number of directors), 128 (Directors to act in good faith), 131 (Failure of directors to cause company to carry on business in a proper manner), 190 (Registered office), 191-196 (Company records and registers); Financial Reporting Act 2013, sections 18-24 (Accounting records and annual reporting)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993, submitted electronically through the New Zealand Companies Office online registration portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. A New Zealand limited company may be incorporated with one or more shares issued for any lawful consideration fixed by the directors. There is no blocked escrow account requirement, no minimum bank balance, and no capital deposit certificate is required before incorporation. Shares may be issued for cash or non-cash consideration, and directors must act in good faith and ensure that the value of the consideration is not inadequate in all the circumstances. Non-resident share ownership is permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY] LIMITED (THE COMPANY) ADOPTED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE COMPANIES ACT 1993. THE DIRECTORS RECORD THAT THE COMPANY WAS DULY INCORPORATED BY THE REGISTRAR OF COMPANIES AND THAT THIS WRITTEN RESOLUTION CONTAINS THE ORGANISATIONAL, GOVERNANCE, BANKING, CAPITAL, AND OFFICER-APPOINTMENT DECISIONS OF THE COMPANY. 1. RATIFICATION OF INCORPORATION AND CONSTITUTION. RESOLVED that the application for registration, the certificate of incorporation, any constitution adopted by the shareholders, and all ancillary filings made with the New Zealand Companies Office be and are hereby ratified, approved, and confirmed in all respects. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARES. RESOLVED that the board of directors authorises and directs the issue and allotment of 1,000 ordinary shares, without par value, or such other number as may be recorded in the share register, to the subscribers named in the share register, credited as fully paid at a consideration of NZ$1.00 per share. RESOLVED FURTHER that the consideration represents fair and reasonable value for the shares, that the directors have complied with all fiduciary duties to the company and its shareholders, and that the board directs completion of the statutory share register and the execution and delivery of share certificates immediately after this meeting. 3. BANKING AUTHORISATION. RESOLVED that the company opens and maintains such banking accounts as the directors may select with one or more New Zealand banks, and that the directors authorised from time to time, or any two of them jointly, be and are hereby appointed signing authorities for the operation of those accounts, including the authority to execute cheques, bank drafts, electronic payment instructions, loan applications, foreign exchange transactions, guarantees, and any related security documents within limits approved by the board. 4. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED that the registered office of the company be fixed and adopted at the physical New Zealand address stated in the Companies Office registration records, and that the statutory registers, minutes, share register, and accounting records of the company be maintained at that office or at such other place as the directors may determine, and that the directors and officers be authorised to file all change-of-address or record notices with the Companies Office. 5. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS. RESOLVED that the following officers be and are hereby appointed: [MANAGING DIRECTOR] as Managing Director, [CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER] as Chief Financial Officer, and [COMPANY SECRETARY] as Company Secretary if the board determines that a secretary is required. RESOLVED FURTHER that the officers are authorised, jointly or severally, to prepare and execute all statutory returns, tax registrations, annual returns, banking instructions, employment contracts, commercial agreements, and regulatory applications required to carry on the company’s marine insurance survey business. 6. STATUTORY COMPLIANCE AND GOVERNANCE. RESOLVED that the company adopts appropriate financial close policies, an anti-money laundering compliance framework if any financial activity is undertaken, a conflicts-of-interest register, and a record-keeping policy in compliance with sections 128, 131, and 191-196 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation, registered office designation, and preparation of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online portal via RealMe at companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the New Zealand Companies Office portal using a verified RealMe identity. Search the Companies Register for identical or confusingly similar names, and obtain a name reservation resolution from the subscribers. Prepare the constitution, confirming objects, share structure, director powers, and shareholder rights in compliance with Companies Act 1993. Confirm the registered office is a physical New Zealand address, not a post office box. Collect the dates of birth, addresses, and signed consents of each intended director and shareholder. For this marine insurance surveying activity, also confirm that the proposed business description includes ISIC 5222 and that directors have no disqualifying insolvency or prohibited-management conditions.
required_dossiers: Verified RealMe identity and NZBN applicant details
Proposed company name and up to three alternative names
Draft constitution, if the company elects to have one under sections 16-21 of the Companies Act 1993
Full names, physical addresses, dates of birth, and signed consent of each proposed director
Proposed registered office (physical New Zealand address, not a PO Box) and postal address
Proposed principal place of business address and business activity description (ISIC 5222)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as indistinguishable or contrary to law, an alternate name may be selected and a new online application made without a second fee in most cases; if the Companies Office queries director consent, correct the digital consent and resubmit within the query window. If the application is suspended for reputational review, submit an adverse-media explanation and supporting evidence to the Companies Office integrity team.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the application for registration under section 12, Companies Act 1993
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the name reservation number and digital consent records, file the statutory application for registration electronically through the Companies Office online portal. Pay the applicable registration fee and receive an immediate receipt; the system will issue the certificate of incorporation and register the company and its directors with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) automatically. Ensure the share structure and director appointments exactly match the consent forms because post-incorporation corrections require separate filings. Retain the electronic certificate of incorporation for all downstream bank, insurer, port-authority, and tax licensing applications. The applicant should also confirm that no third party is used as a serial address without that party’s written consent.
required_dossiers: Completed Companies Office online incorporation application
Name reservation number and NZBN pre-enrolment reference
Signed digital consents of proposed directors and shareholders
Constitution, if adopted
Registered office and principal place of business addresses with landlord or host consent if applicable
Proof of identity documents for each director (valid passport or driver licence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar suspends incorporation for incomplete information, deliver the requested correction through the Companies Office online message system within five business days and, if the certificate is not issued, contact the Companies Office Contact Centre; a fresh application may be required if the original case is closed after prolonged non-response.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Inland Revenue for income tax, GST, PAYE, and employer obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue (New Zealand) via the myIR online platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon incorporation, the Companies Office transmits company and director details to Inland Revenue, which automatically creates an IRD number and an NZBN-linked tax account. The registered officer should log into myIR and confirm the business activity codes, GST registration effective date, and any PAYE or employer obligations. If the company expects to make taxable supplies in New Zealand exceeding NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, GST registration is compulsory and should be elected immediately. The company must also provide bank account details, postal address, director tax residency details, and the intended date of commencement of business. For marine insurance surveying supplied to New Zealand underwriters or overseas principals, confirm whether supplies are subject to GST or may be zero-rated as exported services under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Directors identification and tax residency details
Business activity description and ISIC 5222 classification
Planned GST registration date and forecast annual taxable turnover
Bank account details for Inland Revenue refunds or instalments
Completed IRD business registration forms or online myIR declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number is not generated within five working days, telephone the IRD business line to request a manual cross-check and provide the Companies Office certificate; if GST registration is not backdated correctly, use myIR to correct the effective date and self-assess any interest or penalties before the first return.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting, share allotment, statutory registers, and corporate bank account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The company board of directors and the New Zealand Companies Office for any share allotment or director-change filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass the attached first board written resolution. The board must record the allotment of shares in the share register, issue share certificates, adopt the registered office, and appoint the managing director, chief financial officer, and any company secretary. If the share allotment or officer appointments change any information previously filed on the Companies Register, file the requisite notice online. Execute the bank account application using the board resolution as the corporate authorisation; perform customer due diligence, including beneficial ownership declarations, ultimate controlling interest, and intended transaction profile for marine claims settlement or surveying fees. The bank may require a certified extract of the resolution and proof of physical address.
required_dossiers: Signed first board resolution and minutes or written resolution
Share register, shareholder ledger, and share certificates
Director and officer names, addresses, signatures, and dates of birth
Certificate of incorporation and constitution if any
Bank account application, customer due diligence pack, and proof of physical trading address
AML/CFT compliance questionnaire and beneficial ownership schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank returns the account opening file because of incomplete beneficial ownership data, immediately correct the shareholding percentage table and resubmit; if the Companies Office queries a share allotment notice, rectify the share class or consideration details online and refile before the statutory deadline to avoid a late-filing penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime, workplace health and safety, and premises fire-safety licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Maritime New Zealand, WorkSafe New Zealand, and Fire and Emergency New Zealand for fixed premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess whether the surveyor will perform statutory vessel safety surveys; if so, apply to Maritime New Zealand for recognition as a surveyor or a Recognised Organisation under the Maritime Transport Act 1994. For non-statutory marine cargo and hull claims inspections, obtain professional indemnity insurance, a letter of engagement with the insurer principal, and any relevant port-authority access permits. Establish a health and safety operating system in compliance with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. For any office, store, or survey laboratory, arrange a fire evacuation scheme approval through Fire and Emergency New Zealand and verify that the building warrant of fitness is current. Where inspections occur on vessels or port-controlled areas, coordinate a site-specific hazard assessment with the port operation centre.
required_dossiers: Professional surveyor qualifications and sea-service or underwriting references
Professional indemnity insurance certificate with a limit appropriate to marine cargo values
Maritime New Zealand Surveyor Recognition application or a contractual arrangement with an existing Recognised Organisation
Health and Safety at Work policy, hazard register, and incident response plan
Fire and Emergency New Zealand fire evacuation scheme application and building owner consent for any fixed premises
Port operator access permits where inspections take place on port-controlled areas
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Maritime New Zealand does not recognise the surveyor, submit the application with updated sea-time evidence and a written explanation of the supervisory arrangement to the Maritime NZ marine qualifications review panel; if WorkSafe issues an improvement notice, correct the hazard register and provide staff training records, then request a compliance certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Maritime New Zealand, WorkSafe New Zealand, and the applicable Regional Council or Unitary Authority under the Resource Management Act 1991
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Surveyor Recognition or Authorisation under Maritime Rule 32 and the Maritime Transport Act 1994, together with a Health and Safety at Work compliance system and, for any fixed premises, a Fire Evacuation Scheme approval under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) and the relevant New Zealand Regional Council acting under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Environmental Registration only. Marine cargo and hull claims inspection is a non-discharging field service and does not trigger a full EIA unless a fixed cargo inspection laboratory, warehouse, or washing station is established; if such premises are added, a land-use resource consent and discharge permit may be required under the applicable regional plan.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are generated by inspection activities. If any equipment washing is performed, wash water volume must be less than 5 m3 per day and must not contain free-phase hydrocarbons; any discharge must comply with the applicable regional plan default standards, generally suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L, pH between 6.0 and 9.0, and biochemical oxygen demand not exceeding 20 mg/L. Hazardous substances, including marine debris or cargo residues removed during inspection, must be classified, labelled, and disposed of through a licensed waste transporter under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996 and the Waste Minimisation Act 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A Building Warrant of Fitness and a Fire Evacuation Scheme under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017 must be current for any fixed office, warehouse, or laboratory. The company must also register with WorkSafe New Zealand if it employs workers and carry out a risk assessment of confined-space entry, working near water, fall hazards, manual handling, and site security associated with surveying vessels. No separate Civil Defence emergency licence is required, but the primary duty holder must include emergency response and evacuation arrangements in the Health and Safety at Work system.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) — online portal myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must apply for a New Zealand Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number by lodging the applicable non-resident company registration application through myIR or by post to the IRD. The application package must include certified copies of the company constitution and certificate of incorporation (or equivalent overseas registration evidence), details of the registered office and physical principal place of business, particulars of all directors and shareholders, and confirmation that the company is not resident in New Zealand. The IRD will verify the information and issue the statutory tax identification number (IRD number). To register for Goods and Services Tax (GST), the entity separately files a GST registration application in myIR once turnover meets or is expected to meet the mandatory threshold or if voluntary registration is sought; the IRD will issue a GST registration number linked to the same IRD number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A New Zealand limited company may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status for income tax purposes if it meets the statutory eligibility criteria, effectively permitting shareholders to be taxed on the company's income; however, New Zealand has no US-style check-the-box election. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Acts apply, but no elective hybrid mismatch classification mechanism is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in annual taxable turnover, measured over any 12-month period, or NZD 60,000 projected for the next 12 months; offshore suppliers of remote services to New Zealand consumers face the same NZD 60,000 registration threshold under the offshore supplier registration regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or anti-fraud digital stamping. E-invoicing operates on a voluntary basis using the New Zealand E-Invoicing framework built on the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 standard. GST returns and remittances must be filed electronically through myIR, and all GST records must be retained in accordance with the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and the Tax Administration Act 1994.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for GST applies to exports of goods where the supplier provides the goods and they are exported by the supplier or an agent within 28 days of the time of supply. Export services, including qualifying marine insurance survey and cargo claim inspection services supplied to a non-resident underwriter, insurer, carrier, or overseas principal, may be zero-rated if the statutory tests under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 are satisfied, including the supply being made to a person who is not resident in New Zealand and the services not falling within a standard-rated exception (such as services supplied in connection with land in New Zealand or certain moveable property physically situated in New Zealand unless a specific exclusion applies). The supplier must retain contemporaneous records evidencing the export transaction, the non-resident status of the recipient, the commercial purpose of the supply, and the cross-border foreign-exchange payment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration in the New Zealand Trade Single Window (NZWarehouse) or equivalent customs clearance evidence showing goods exported
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export and delivery outside New Zealand
Commercial invoice and underlying contract or survey engagement order
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank foreign-exchange receipt evidencing payment in foreign currency from the overseas recipient
Marine survey report and cargo/vessel claim inspection certificate demonstrating the nature of the exported service supplied
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If a zero-rated export claim is overturned on audit through inadequate documentation, fraudulent documentation, or failure to meet the statutory export test, the IRD will assess GST at 15% and claw back any refunded or previously offset tax. Use-of-money interest applies from the original due date. Penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 include shortfall penalties of up to 100% for gross carelessness, substantial understatement, or taking an abusive tax position, and up to 150% for evasion or fraudulent intent, with additional criminal sanctions for knowingly providing false tax returns. Directors and controlling shareholders may be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid GST and penalties where the company has failed to comply with tax obligations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand - Te Putea Matua, central bank; New Zealand maintains no separate foreign-exchange-control administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalized financial system under IMF Article VIII obligations, meaning the New Zealand dollar is fully convertible for both current and capital account purposes. There are no restrictions on the purchase, sale, or transfer of foreign exchange, no surrender requirements on export proceeds, and no prior Reserve Bank approval for cross-border capital movements. The current account is completely free for trade in goods and services, including marine survey fees, insurance premiums, and claim settlement flows. The capital account permits foreign direct investment, portfolio investment, intercompany loans, share subscriptions, and profit distributions without exchange-control approval, although certain overseas investment transactions may require consent under the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which is a foreign-ownership screening regime rather than a currency control. In practice, profit remittances from a New Zealand limited company face only normal withholding tax obligations, non-resident withholding tax on dividends or interest, and bank-level AML/CFT documentation checks. There is no central bank approval queue, no repatriation delay, and no mandatory FX surrender. Corporate treasurers can freely convert NZD and retain export earnings in foreign currency. The only practical hurdles are regulatory compliance, tax filing, and standard banking due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no export proceeds surrender rules in New Zealand. Exporters are not required to convert export receipts into NZD within any statutory timeline and may hold foreign currency indefinitely in bank accounts. There are no mandatory conversion ratios. Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, the banking relationship must satisfy origin-of-funds and trade-evidence checks, but no exchange-control surrender deadline applies. The statutory position is full retention.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Trade Finance Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMIs such as Wise are viable as auxiliary payment rails rather than principal banking infrastructure. Wise Payments NZ Limited is registered as a financial service provider under the Financial Service Providers Registration and Dispute Resolution Act 2008 and is covered by a dispute resolution scheme, but it is not a registered bank and cannot provide commercial lending, deposit-taking products, bank guarantees, or in-branch treasury services. EMIs are legally permitted to serve New Zealand entities for global payment collection and FX conversion, provided they are not marketed as banks. For a marine insurance surveyor, an EMI can be used for receiving premium refunds or claim disbursements in low volume, but capital verification, intercompany loan governance, and large marine insurance settlements should flow through tier-1 domestic banks. A significant constraint is that banks and underwriters may reject EMI statements as source-of-funds evidence because EMI transaction records do not always carry full SWIFT originator information. Therefore, the cross-border viability rating is Medium as an operational convenience and Low as a compliance-complete treasury or clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not required by New Zealand statute to attend a physical bank branch to open a corporate account, but the AML/CFT regime requires banks to identify directors and beneficial owners. Most tier-1 banks require at least one director or authorized signatory to complete face-to-face identity verification; for non-resident directors, banks generally accept a remote video interview combined with notarized or apostilled certified copies and original company documents delivered via registered post. Consular proxy opening is not a statutory right and depends on bank policy. To achieve High onboarding viability, use a New Zealand registered agent, provide complete Companies Office extract, and have at least one local director available for branch or video verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore trust or opaque ownership chain where the ultimate beneficial owner cannot be identified from the Companies Office extract, especially if a foreign trust holds the surveying company shares.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chronological share register, trust deed and material trust resolutions, sworn declaration of beneficial ownership from the trustee, certified passports of all natural persons in the ownership chain, audited or unaudited financial statements, AML/CFT due diligence file of the professional accountant, and a register of controllers filed under the New Zealand Companies Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions referencing sanctioned jurisdictions, high-risk vessel flags, or marine survey engagements for vessels operating in sanctioned territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening policy documentation, sanctions search results for all counterparties, vessel IMO numbers, AIS tracking positions, bills of lading and cargo manifests, protection and indemnity insurance certificate, surveyor engagement contracts, written memorandum confirming no sanctioned parties, and a granular SWIFT audit trail with beneficiary details.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for share capital or intercompany loans from a third party or related party in a different jurisdiction, creating a source-of-wealth blocker.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds statement signed by the remitter, remitting bank reference letter, six-month bank statements, audited financial statements of the lending entity, executed intercompany loan agreement with commercial interest rate, tax invoice, New Zealand tax compliance certificate, and a chartered accountant capital verification report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of recognized marine surveying occupational credentials, causing the bank to question whether the entity is a shell company rather than a legitimate surveyor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Marine surveyor licenses and professional registration from recognized bodies such as the International Institute of Marine Surveying or NZ Marine Survey Services, professional indemnity insurance certificate, client contracts, corporate website and business email domain, staffing and office lease documentation, and Maritime New Zealand licensing endorsement where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections should use SWIFT MT103 from the overseas remitting bank to the New Zealand bank SWIFT BIC, with the beneficiary account in the company name and reference clearly stating SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION or INTERCOMPANY LOAN. Since New Zealand has no exchange control, no Reserve Bank filing is required. The company must still issue shares and record the issuance in the shareholders register, file an annual return with the New Zealand Companies Office, and produce a board resolution authorizing the share issuance. For an intercompany loan, execute a facility agreement and account for non-resident interest withholding tax. Capital verification can be performed by a New Zealand chartered accountant reviewing the bank statement, share register, and business plan, producing a verification letter for underwriters and counterparties. If funds originate from a bank-secrecy jurisdiction, include a corresponding bank attestation and a complete pre-funding KYC pack.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 for routine marine survey fees, insurer refunds, and claim payments, referencing the invoice and engagement contract. For larger cargo claim settlements, use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued by the counterparty bank and confirmed by a New Zealand tier-1 bank, or documentary collections with sight drafts under ICC URC 522 or UCP 600. The domestic NZD leg is cleared through the New Zealand Exchange Settlement Account System, while the cross-border leg is executed via SWIFT. All outbound payments require standard AML/CFT screening, sanctions screening, and beneficiary account title matching before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts with registered banks for USD, AUD, EUR, GBP, and JPY, limited to documented underlying trade or claim exposure
Non-deliverable forward contracts for currencies without a deep deliverable New Zealand market, structured through the banks offshore desk and subject to credit and margin approval
Cross-currency swaps for long-term intercompany debt with maturity above 12 months, limited to balance-sheet hedging and approved by bank treasury risk committees
Plain-vanilla currency options for large tender and marine salvage exposure, but speculative uncovered FX transactions are not permitted under standard banking facility terms

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the company's Annual Return Date, being the last day of the month in which each anniversary of incorporation falls; the Registrar issues a reminder to the registered office before the due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 100 (approximately USD 60); continued non-compliance triggers a formal written notice requiring delivery within 20 working days; failure to comply leads to a Gazette notice of proposed removal and administrative strike-off from the New Zealand Companies Register, after which restoration requires a court order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Independent Audit Report (if triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and, for large or FMC reporting entities, the Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the balance date under section 210 of the Companies Act 1993; the audit report, where required, must accompany the financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or file financial statements may result in monetary penalties under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, director-specific civil liability, possible infringement notice enforcement, and continued default may lead to prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 7 July following a 31 March balance date for the standard New Zealand tax year; terminal tax is due by 7 February after the tax year unless a tax agent extension applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: NZD 250 initial late filing penalty, further NZD 50 per month up to NZD 500, plus use-of-money interest on unpaid tax and a 4% late payment penalty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the 28th day of the month following the end of the taxable period; for six-monthly filers, returns are due within 28 days after each six-month period, typically covering 31 March and 30 September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250, additional NZD 50 per month up to NZD 500, a 4% late payment penalty on the unpaid GST, and use-of-money interest on overdue amounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer Payday Filing (PAYE / KiwiSaver / ESCT) if the Company has employees or director payroll
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two working days after each payday throughout the income year; final period ending 31 March is reconciled with the employer annual schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payday filing penalties of NZD 250 initially, plus NZD 50 per month; unpaid employee deductions attract employer penalties, late payment penalties, and use-of-money interest

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit is legally required if the company, together with its subsidiaries, exceeds any one of the following at balance date: total assets in excess of NZD 60 million; total revenue in excess of NZD 30 million; or 50 or more full-time equivalent employees. Audit is also compulsory for FMC reporting entities under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, for publicly accountable entities, where the constitution requires an audit, or where shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares validly request an audit under the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalent to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) for Tier 1 for-profit entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) for eligible Tier 2 entities; Simple Format Reporting (SFR) under Tier 3 or Tier 4 for smaller non-complex private entities; all applied under the XRB Accounting Standards Framework, the Financial Reporting Act 2013, and Part 7 of the Companies Act 1993.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Significant Controller Register and include a confirmation statement in the Annual Return. Significant control changes must be recorded in the register within 10 working days of becoming aware of the change. For share transfers, the directors must register a valid instrument of transfer in the Register of Members within 30 days of receipt, and the updated shareholding structure is confirmed annually by the director signing the Annual Return. The company must take reasonable steps to identify all significant controllers holding more than 25% ownership or control and must notify the Companies Office of any required register statement within the prescribed filing timeline.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Minutes of Shareholder and Director Meetings)
Significant Controller Register (where a significant control relationship exists)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 18,000 per annum for a triggered statutory audit engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not operate free-zone or patent-box regimes. The principal incentive is the R&D Tax Incentive, a 15% credit on eligible R&D expenditure, subject to IRD pre-approval and quantum caps.
